newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran rejects Amnesty charges of human rights abuse.
newsitem.headline: Iran rejects Amnesty charges of human rights abuse.

text.p: A senior Iranian official on Monday rejected out of hand recent Amnesty International allegations of human rights abuses in the Islamic republic, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
Deputy judiciary chief Mohammad Reza Abbasi-Fard said allegations of maltreatment of prisoners and miscarriages of justice in Iran were "utterly false", IRNA reported.
Amnesty International accused Iran on June 3 of human rights violations against prominent dissident Shi'ite Moslem clerics and their followers.
The London-based human rights group said at least three senior religious figures were reportedly being held under house arrest, and that their followers had been detained and reportedly tortured.
But Abbasi-Fard was quoted as saying that some of the incidents described as torture by Amnesty International were punishments which Iran levied for certain felonies.

He added that Iran's judiciary would not allow any person to "take advantage of political or religious liberties as a means for engaging in acts against national security or against the nation and do so with impunity", IRNA said.
